'''Leonard Hyman Soicher''' is a British-Canadian [[mathematics|mathematician]] who worked in [[algebraic graph theory]], [[group theory]], [[combinatorial design theory]], and [[Discrete_mathematics#Theoretical_computer_science|discrete computational mathematics]].
He is an [[Emeritus]] Professor of Mathematics at [[Queen Mary University of London]].<ref>https://www.qmul.ac.uk/maths/profiles/soicherlh.html</ref>

== Education ==

Soicher earned a [[BSc]] in mathematics in 1978 and a [[Master of Computer Science]] in 1981,<ref name = "not a duplicate"/> both from [[Concordia University]] in Montreal, Canada.
His master's [[thesis]], titled “The Computation of Galois groups”, was supervised by [[John McKay (mathematician)|John McKay]].<ref name = "not a duplicate">https://central.bac-lac.gc.ca/.item?id=TC-QMG-4916&op=pdf&app=Library&oclc_number=1033219418</ref>
He won a [[Cambridge_Commonwealth_Trust|Commonwealth Scholarship]]<ref name = "repeat">{{cite thesis | last1=Soicher | first1=Leonard | title=Presentations of Some Finite Groups | date=2024 | publisher=Apollo - University of Cambridge Repository | doi=10.17863/CAM.110463 | url=https://doi.org/10.17863/CAM.110463 }}</ref> to pursue a [[PhD|doctorate]] from the [[University of Cambridge]], with [[John H. Conway]] as his supervisor.<ref>{{cite web | title=Leonard Soicher - the Mathematics Genealogy Project | url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=71375 }}</ref>
Soicher was awarded his PhD in 1985, with a PhD [[thesis]] titled “Presentations of Some Finite Groups”<ref name = "repeat"/> that focused on sporadic simple groups.

== Career ==

Soicher has worked across a range of fields as a professional pure mathematician.
After his doctorate, he worked again with [[John McKay (mathematician)|John McKay]] as a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoc]] at Concordia University in Canada.<ref>LMS Newsletter, Issue 503, November 2022, Pages 44–45. https://www.lms.ac.uk/sites/default/files/inline-files/NLMS_503_for%20web_0.pdf</ref>
He then joined [[Queen Mary University of London]] in 1987, where he remained until retirement in 2018, becoming a [[Professor]] in 2007.<ref>https://www.qmul.ac.uk/maths/news-and-events/news-/items/professor-leonard-soicher-inaugural-lecture.html</ref>

Soicher is most known for his early work on presentations of sporadic simple groups; his contribution to the [[ATLAS of Finite Groups]]; the [[Bimonster group]]; work with [[Charles Leedham-Green]] developing “collection from the left”<ref>Collection from the left and other strategies, C.R. Leedham-Green, L.H. Soicher, Journal of Symbolic Computation, Volume 9, Issues 5–6, 1990, Pages 665-675,
https://doi.org/10.1016/S0747-7171(08)80081-8</ref> and the product replacement algorithm.<ref> The product replacement algorithm is polynomial, Igor Pak, Proc. FOCS 2000, 41st Annual Symposium, 476-485, https://www.math.ucla.edu/~pak/papers/PRfocs6.pdf</ref><ref>https://web.archive.org/web/20040911211017/http://citeseer.ist.psu.edu/390703.html</ref> in [[computational group theory]]; his research on distance-regular graphs (especially the three so-called Soicher graphs<ref>{{cite web | title=Soicher Graphs | url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/SoicherGraphs.html }}</ref><ref>Three New Distance-regular Graphs,
Leonard H. Soicher, European Journal of Combinatorics, Volume 14, Issue 5, 1993, Pages 501-505,
https://doi.org/10.1006/eujc.1993.1052.</ref> and the Moscow-Soicher graph<ref>{{cite web | title=Moscow-Soicher Graph | url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/Moscow-SoicherGraph.html }}</ref><ref>Yet Another Distance Regular Graph Related to a Golay Code, Leonard H. Soicher, The Electronic Journal of Combinatorics, Volume 2, Issue 1, 1995, https://doi.org/10.37236/1220</ref>); and his long-term and ongoing authorship and development of the GRAPE package<ref>{{cite web | title=GAP package GRAPE | url=https://gap-packages.github.io/grape }}</ref> for [[GAP (computer algebra system)|GAP]]. Soicher is also a co-creator and maintainer of the website [https://www.designtheory.org ''designtheory.org''].

Soicher has co-published with notable mathematicians, including [[Peter Cameron (mathematician)|Peter Cameron]], [[John Conway]], [[Simon P. Norton]], [[Cheryl Praeger]], and [[Sarah Rees (professor)|Sarah Rees]]<ref>{{cite web | title=Google Scholar | url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=8jNMqycAAAAJ }}</ref>

== GAP ==

Soicher has been a member of the council of the computer algebra system [[GAP (computer algebra system)|GAP]] since June 1997, and was its chair from March 2009 until September 2021.<ref>{{cite web | title=Council | url=https://www.gap-system.org/council }}</ref>
He is the author of the GRAPE<ref>{{cite web | title=GAP package GRAPE | url=https://gap-packages.github.io/grape }}</ref> and DESIGN<ref>{{cite web | title=GAP package DESIGN | url=https://gap-packages.github.io/design }}</ref> packages for GAP.
A special session in honour of Soicher's 70th birthday was held at the GAP Days Summer 2025 workshop in Koper, Slovenia.<ref>{{cite web | title=Program · GAP Days Summer 2025 | url=https://www.gapdays.de/gapdays2025-summer/program/ }}</ref>

== Selected publications ==
* with John McKay: [https://doi.org/10.1016/0022-314X(85)90022-8 ''Computing Galois groups over the rationals''], Journal of Number Theory (1985).
* with John H. Conway, Simon P. Norton: ''The Bimonster, the group ''Y''<sub>555</sub>, and the projective plane of order 3'', Computers in Algebra (1988).
* with Rosemary A. Bailey, Peter J. Cameron, Peter Dobcsányi, John P. Morgan: [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.disc.2004.10.027 ''Designs on the web''], Discrete Mathematics (2006).
* with Cheryl E. Praeger: [https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511526039 ''Low rank representations and graphs for sporadic groups''], Cambridge University Press (1996).
